How do you train a dog to be a guard dog?

A large part of this is going to be the breed you choose.

Dobermans, German Shepherds, Great Pyrenees, all excellent guard dogs with minimal training, and they're generally great with people they trust and know. They all have their downsides, from temperament issues (fucking Dobermans) to sheer size (Pyrenees), so you're going to have to really take a look at your situation, do some research, and find out what dog is going be your best fit. After that, it's just training like regular.

You don't, really, want your dog to attack anybody. Kids and shit can always wander into your vicinity accidentally, then your dog gets put down. You want your dog to put on the pretense of attacking. Teeth bared, ears back, growl, etc. While it's not hard to do, I would recommend a professional trainer to do that part for you. It's hard, sometimes, to clearly mark that line of 'act not attack'. If you have the means to do it professionally, it won't take long. Maybe a week or two of training, if you get a dog that's a little quicker.

Just remember, your dog is a deterrent at most. If somebody wants in while you're not around, they'll get in regardless.

Just my experience in training dogs:

-Female dogs usually make better guards.

-A small dog and a large dog are a good pairing for home defense. Large dogs can be lazy but a smaller panicky guy will alert them of things that require attention. -You are looking for a personality not a breed.

-It is easier to teach a yappy dog to bark less than it is to teach a quiet dog to bark more.

-The key to having a good guard dog is teaching the dog what to bark at and don't be a lazy fuck and not verify threats.

For example: Person walks past yard. Dog barks. Instead of just telling dog to shut up, you get up, verify that someone has indeed walked in the yard and then tell dog that it's okay. If someone walks through your yard and dog barks, make a big deal about it, get up and verify threat and reward the dog.

Over time, dog will learn about what are threats to be concerned with and things not to be concerned with. Dogs also have different barks they use for people they know, strangers, other animals, proximity violations, etc.

If you want a dog that will know when and how to bite, you need a smart independent dog that views you as a partner. A dog will not risk it's health and safety for a master but it will for a friend.

If you truly wanted a guard dog you'd have to look at buying a trained one or getting into the training. Something like Schutzhund.
